html:
Day of about twenty bomb attacks across Belfast by the Provisional IRA, on 21 July 1972. Nine people died and some 130 were hurt.

The bombs went off over about 80 minutes, in the city centre, at a bus station, and at shops and railway stations. Warnings were given, but they were too late or confused, and the crowded streets made it hard to clear people in time. Pictures of body parts being shovelled from the road shocked the world.

The attack came three weeks after a short ceasefire collapsed and only months after Bloody Sunday. It cost the IRA public sympathy, and soon after the British Army launched Operation Motorman to retake the no-go areas of Belfast and Derry. See the-troubles.
sum: Day of about twenty bomb attacks across Belfast by the Provisional IRA, on 21 July 1972. Nine people died and some 130 were hurt.
